commonMistake: Client-rendering important content.
interviewTip: Mention generateSitemaps for very large catalogs.

question: How would you implement a modal with a shareable URL in the App Router?
shortAnswer: Combine a parallel route slot (@modal) with an intercepting route so soft navigation shows a modal and hard navigation shows the full page.
detailedAnswer: The layout renders {children} and {modal}. @modal/(.)photo/[id]/page.tsx renders the modal on Link navigation; photo/[id]/page.tsx renders the full page on refresh. @modal/default.tsx returns null. Close with router.back().
commonMistake: Managing the modal with client state only, losing deep links.
interviewTip: Draw the folder structure.

question: What problems can arise from caching in Next.js and how do you debug them?
shortAnswer: Stale data after mutations, personalized data cached globally, and confusion across cache layers; debug by checking which layer served the data and whether invalidation ran.
detailedAnswer: Check if the route is static or dynamic (build output), whether fetches are cached, whether tags match between cacheTag/fetch and revalidateTag, and whether the client router cache is holding old payloads (router.refresh). Log cache behaviour, use the Next.js dev overlay and build output, and make caching explicit and documented.
commonMistake: Disabling all caching to fix a bug.
interviewTip: Give a concrete stale-after-update story.

question: How would you implement infinite scrolling with Server Components and Server Actions or Route Handlers?
shortAnswer: Render the first page on the server, then fetch subsequent pages from the client via a Route Handler, Server Function or library, appending results.
detailedAnswer: The initial list is server-rendered for SEO and speed. A Client Component observes the last item (IntersectionObserver) and loads the next page with cursor-based pagination, using TanStack Query's useInfiniteQuery or a Server Function that returns serializable data. Keep the URL in sync if needed and virtualize long lists.
commonMistake: Fetching all items at once.
interviewTip: Mention cursor vs offset pagination trade-offs.

question: When would you use the Edge runtime vs the Node.js runtime?
shortAnswer: Default to Node.js for full compatibility; use edge for lightweight, latency-sensitive logic without Node-only dependencies.
detailedAnswer: Edge has fast startup and runs near users but supports a subset of APIs and many npm packages won't work. If the function talks to a single-region database, edge can add latency. Node.js supports everything, including ORMs and native modules. Next 16's proxy runs on Node.js.
commonMistake: Moving database-heavy routes to the edge for 'speed'.
interviewTip: Bring up data locality.

question: How would you migrate a Pages Router app to the App Router?
shortAnswer: Incrementally: add app/ alongside pages/, move routes one by one, convert data functions to async Server Components, and replace API routes and _app logic.
detailedAnswer: Start with a root layout replacing _app/_document. Migrate simple pages first. getStaticProps → cached Server Component fetching; getServerSideProps → dynamic Server Component; getStaticPaths → generateStaticParams; useRouter from next/router → next/navigation hooks; API routes → Route Handlers or Server Actions; head tags → Metadata API. Watch for 'use client' needs in interactive components and test each route.
commonMistake: Big-bang migration of the entire app.
interviewTip: Show the concept mapping table.

question: How do you secure a Next.js application end to end?
shortAnswer: Authenticate with a vetted library, authorize in a server-only DAL, validate all inputs, protect secrets, set security headers and keep dependencies updated.
detailedAnswer: Use httpOnly secure cookies, verify sessions in every Server Action and Route Handler, return DTOs, sanitize HTML, add CSP/HSTS headers, rate-limit auth endpoints, avoid NEXT_PUBLIC_ secrets, audit dependencies, and monitor errors. Don't rely solely on proxy for auth.
commonMistake: Securing only the UI.
interviewTip: Organize the answer by layer.

question: How would you monitor a Next.js app in production?
shortAnswer: Instrument with OpenTelemetry via instrumentation.ts, report errors with onRequestError, collect real-user Web Vitals and log key events with after().
detailedAnswer: Track server traces for slow data fetches, error rates per route, cache hit rates, Server Action failures, and client metrics (LCP, INP, CLS) via useReportWebVitals or a vendor SDK. Use after() for non-blocking analytics and alert on regressions.
commonMistake: Only monitoring uptime.
interviewTip: Mention tying traces to deployments.

question: How would you share data between a layout and its pages without prop drilling?
shortAnswer: Fetch in each place that needs the data using a memoized function (fetch memoization or React cache()); layouts can't pass props to pages.
detailedAnswer: Because layouts render children without props, call getUser() in both layout and page — request memoization ensures one query. For client-side sharing, put a Context provider (client) in the layout and pass the server-fetched value to it.
keyPoints: Layouts can't pass props to pages
commonMistake: Trying to clone children with extra props in a layout.
interviewTip: Explain request-scoped memoization.

question: How does Next.js decide whether a route is static or dynamic?
shortAnswer: During build it tries to prerender; if code accesses request-time APIs or uncached data, the route (or that part) becomes dynamic.
detailedAnswer: Dynamic APIs (cookies, headers, searchParams, connection, draftMode) and uncached fetches opt in to request-time rendering. Route segment config (dynamic, revalidate) can force behaviour in the classic model. With Cache Components, Next.js prerenders everything it can into a shell and requires Suspense around dynamic access. The build output shows each route's type.
commonMistake: Not realizing a deep child reading searchParams makes the route dynamic.
interviewTip: Mention reading the build output.

question: How would you build a multi-step form with Server Actions?
shortAnswer: Keep step state on the client (or in the URL), validate each step with server-side schemas, persist drafts if needed, and submit the final data with a Server Action.
detailedAnswer: Client state (useReducer) holds progress; each step can call a Server Action to validate partial data and return errors. Use the URL (searchParams) for step navigation to support back/refresh. Final submission revalidates and redirects. Validate the full payload again on the server at the end.
commonMistake: Trusting earlier step validation on final submit.
interviewTip: Mention useActionState per step.

question: How do you minimize client JavaScript in a Next.js app?
shortAnswer: Keep components on the server, push 'use client' to small leaves, lazy-load heavy widgets and audit bundles.
detailedAnswer: Use the children pattern to keep providers thin, avoid client-only libraries for static UI, use next/dynamic for rarely used components, configure optimizePackageImports, enable the React Compiler for runtime efficiency, and analyze bundles regularly.
commonMistake: Converting whole pages to client components for convenience.
interviewTip: Quantify impact with bundle analyzer results.

question: Explain the difference between revalidateTag and updateTag in Next.js 16.
shortAnswer: revalidateTag marks data stale with stale-while-revalidate semantics (requires a cacheLife profile); updateTag immediately expires data and is only available in Server Actions for read-your-writes.
detailedAnswer: Use revalidateTag('posts', 'max') from webhooks or background jobs where serving slightly stale content while refreshing is fine. Use updateTag('posts') right after a user's own mutation so their next render shows the change. refresh() refreshes uncached data on the client router.
commonMistake: Using revalidateTag after a user edit and showing them stale data.
interviewTip: Tie it to user experience expectations.

question: How does streaming affect HTTP status codes, redirects and SEO in Next.js?
shortAnswer: Once streaming starts the 200 status and headers are already sent, so later notFound() or redirect() calls are handled by injecting client-side instructions; crawlers still receive the full streamed HTML.
detailedAnswer: Call notFound() and redirect() before any Suspense boundary starts streaming (e.g. at the top of the page) when the status code matters. Inside streamed content, Next.js inserts a meta tag or script to redirect or show the not-found UI. Streamed HTML is complete when the response finishes, so content is indexable, and metadata can be streamed for browsers while still placed in the head for bots.
commonMistake: Calling notFound() deep inside a Suspense boundary and expecting a 404 status.
interviewTip: Explain why ordering of checks matters for SEO-critical pages.

question: How would you handle real-time data (e.g. live notifications) in a Next.js App Router app?
shortAnswer: Render initial data on the server, then subscribe on the client via WebSockets, Server-Sent Events or a hosted real-time service, merging updates into client state.
detailedAnswer: Server Components provide the initial snapshot for fast, SEO-friendly HTML. A Client Component opens a subscription in useEffect (with cleanup) or uses useSyncExternalStore around a socket store. Serverless platforms often require a managed real-time provider (Pusher, Ably, Supabase Realtime) because long-lived connections aren't supported. Call router.refresh() or revalidate tags when events affect server-rendered data.
commonMistake: Polling Server Actions in a tight loop.
interviewTip: Mention connection limits of serverless functions.

question: How would you design a multi-tenant SaaS on Next.js?
shortAnswer: Resolve the tenant early (subdomain or path) in proxy, carry the tenant id through a server-only context, and scope every query and cache key by tenant.
detailedAnswer: Proxy rewrites tenant subdomains to a [tenant] segment. The DAL reads the tenant from params and the session, verifies membership, and filters queries by tenant id. Cache tags and 'use cache' keys must include the tenant to avoid cross-tenant leaks. Per-tenant metadata and theming come from cached tenant config. Add row-level security in the database as defense in depth.
commonMistake: Caching tenant data without the tenant in the key.
interviewTip: Emphasize data isolation and cache keys.
